text.p: Winterthur Insurance Co finance director Erwin Heri said the company was too conservative when it forecast in October that 1996 profit would grow by double digits.
"We indicated at our autumn news conference that we should show double-digit profit growth," he told the Finanz und Wirtschaft newspaper in an interview published on Saturday.

"Nothing has changed about this estimate. First indications show us, however, that we were rather too conservative in the autumn," he said without elaborating. Group net rose 15.1 percent in 1995 to 419.2 million Swiss francs.

Heri also said the company's asset allocation was little changed from what it published in its previous annual report, but added it had expandded its international diversification in the spring in light of low Swiss franc interest rates.
"It is clear that the marked weakening of the Swiss franc, especially in the second half of the year, had a positive impact," he said.

He said he company's annual profit growth of 15 to 20 percent since 1992 should have done more for its share price, adding he could not give the source of renewed buying interest recently because share registration requests had not arrived.
"We are hearing that a Swiss bank on the exchange seems to have large orders, but also note that we have been more broadly recommended in the past few days."
